title: Us vs Them
idea: Brief #12 (Briefs for HS, tab #12). 1:1 swipe of the Nuzzy Pen skin tag ad (46 days live): "taking the world by storm" trend hook → old way (skin clinics 👎, $200+, weeks of waiting) vs new way (Haven & Spool 👍) → demo + mechanism → features → review proof → Buy 3 Get 3 → CTA. The first 6-7 s is a Day 1 → Day 5 → Day 14 montage of one skin tag drying and falling off, ending on the dried tag held in her palm: result promised in the first second, the #1 pattern across our skin tag winners (#7, #182, #78, #156). The old way/new way split is a format none of our skin tag ads use yet. Backed by Nuzzy (46 days), our skin tag winners #78 ($2.5k) and #156, #189's 3D mechanism look, and #181's free-bottle hook image.

script.script: BOTH HOOKS, same spoken line: This skin tag remover is taking the world by storm. Thousands of women are getting rid of their skin tags at home for the first time, and I finally get why.
script.visual:
Only the initial image changes (about 1 to 1.5 s), then every hook goes into the same DAY MONTAGE.
H1 initial image (copy the reference's first frame, ref 0:00-0:05): she's lying back with her head turned to the side like the woman on the clinic bed, extreme macro of a small skin tag on the side of her neck.

H2 initial image = ONE STILL IMAGE (not a clip, no movement): the exact frame from our #181 Hook 2: hands lifting one of our amber bottles out of an open shipping box full of our bottles, with the #181 top banner on it. Hold it about 1 s, then cut into the montage.
DAY MONTAGE (about 6 s, all hooks, under the rest of the VO line, then into "The old way?"): ONE woman, ONE skin tag, filmed the exact same way in every clip: lying back, head turned to the side (same as ref 0:00-0:05), extreme macro on the tag on the side of her neck, same angle, spot and light, so it reads as one tag over time.
1) DAY 1 (about 1.5 s): normal skin colour; our rose quartz ball rolls right over it and leaves a glossy oil sheen.
2) DAY 5 (about 1.5 s): same tag, noticeably darker and drier, starting to shrivel.
3) DAY 14 (about 1.5 s): same spot, the tag is gone, smooth skin.
4) Payoff (about 1.5 s): her fingertips hold the tiny dark, shriveled tag up to the camera in her palm, our amber bottle out of focus behind it.
Real-life references: framing = ref 0:00-0:05; DAY progression + labels = our #78 and #332; the drying look = #189's 3D shot.

H1 (on the initial image only): this skin tag remover (small white caption like the reference)

editing_notes:

HOOKS: 2 hooks, one spoken line; only the initial image changes. H1 initial image = Nuzzy's own first frame (46 days). H2 initial image = a STILL IMAGE only (not a video clip): our launched #181's Hook 2 frame (the "50% OFF + A FREE BOTTLE" banner over hands lifting a bottle out of a shipping box full of bottles), our own offer winner: https://hyperscale.ceo/briefs/8ecb83f7-9ba4-433a-8c05-a3ccc6481739 The DAY montage = our #78 (DAY 1 to DAY 4, $2.5k) + #332, framed like the reference's opening shot.
FRAME BY FRAME: copy the reference timestamp in each Visual cell. Where the reference shows THEIR pen zapping skin, show OUR roller rolling over the same spot with the same framing. Never show their product, their logo or a plasma pen. Our bottle and roller = real product photos (Products tab).
C6-0:22) is the heartOMPARISON SECTION (ref 0:0 of the ad: big title box "Skin Clinics 👎", boxes stack one at a time on the VO ("Costs $200+", "Weeks-long wait times"); then the title flips to "Haven & Spool 👍" and boxes stack again ("Cold-pressed organic castor oil", "Use it from the comfort of home", "Soaks down to the root", "No appointments", "No $200 bills").
CAPTIONS: each hook's text sits ONLY on its own initial image (about 1 to 1.5 s); once the DAY montage starts the ONLY text is the big bold white DAY label (DAY 1 → DAY 5 → DAY 14), no captions. After the montage: small white lowercase captions centred low, like the reference.
B-ROLL: ALL B-ROLL, no talking head at all (no one talks to camera, no lip-sync). Real-looking AI UGC hands, necks and skin close-ups + one 3D shot + a review collage, one clean shot per line like the reference.
SOCIAL PROOF (ref 0:45-0:50): a fanned collage of REAL text-review screenshots from our Skin Tags page (havenspool.co, 4,000+ five-star reviews site-wide). No customer skin tag photos. Never write fake comments.
CLAIMS: "cuts off its blood supply... dries out and falls off" = the wording of our launched #156 (a removal claim). Softer back-up line if Meta rejects it: "...so it dries out and shrinks on its own." Skin tags ONLY: no moles or pigmentation.
OFFER: Buy 3 Get 3 Free (6 bottles for $144 = $24 a bottle, half price) + "if the tag's still there, you get a refund" (Skin Tags page). Landing page: Skin Tags page with Buy 3 Get 3 selected.
Doc: Briefs for HS, tab #12.

Voiceover: THE MOST IMPORTANT PART OF THIS AD. It must sound like a real woman, not AI: female, 40s to 50s, casual and excited like she's telling a friend about a find, natural breaths, little laughs, uneven pacing, real emphasis on "how satisfying is that?". If it sounds even slightly robotic, redo it. Match the reference's pace: about 55 to 60 s, punchy short lines. NEEDS TO HAVE CONVICTION in their voice, its boring to listen to a dull script. They need to speak with character.

Avatar: No talking head. Real-looking AI UGC women 45 to 60 (our buyer) shown only through B-roll: hands, necks, underarms, a woman checking her neck in the bathroom mirror, a hand holding our bottle. Filmed-on-a-phone look, at home, natural light. Small, realistic skin tags (side of the neck, under the arm, near the eye, on the chest). Real skin texture, no gore. Clinic scene (ref 0:06-0:11): esthetician in black scrubs treating a woman on a clinic bed, same framing as the reference.
